text:
Course Code: HIS101
Faculty: SLN
I usually don't pay much attention to student reviews about faculties. Over six semesters, I've taken many courses with teachers who had bad reviews, and I usually gave them the benefit of the doubt. Sometimes it worked out, sometimes it didnt. I've rarely written negative reviews before because Ive always felt that if I had tried harder or done something differently, I could have improved my performance.
With SLN I went in with the same mindset. I prepared thoroughly, studied hard, and gave my best effort in quizzes, presentation, and exams. I thought that showing dedication and understanding the material would be enough to succeed. 
But what became clear quickly is that she treats students' efforts not as something to encourage but as a challenge. When students genuinely try their best, she seems to feel insecure and, instead of appreciating the work, becomes demeaning or condescending. Even when answers are mostly correct, she often dismisses them or criticizes unnecessarily. I have personally seen cases where students who should have received full marks didn't, despite their answers being correct.
The classroom environment reflects this as well. More than half the class tries to see something good in her, but they've basically given up because they know putting in effort won't change the outcome. They don't care about their grades because the system feels unfair. Some of us still care a lot about our grades and try to do our best, but it's exhausting when effort alone doesn't seem to be enough. Eventually, when grades are released, I think many still glazing her will realize that no amount of convincing themselves that she's "good' can change the reality of how their work is graded.
I really admire the students who manage not to let her affect them, who stay confident and don't let her criticism shake them. That's something I respect a lot, because I've seen how she can get to students, including me and others. It's not easy to stay unaffected in this class, and it's impressive when someone does.
I have noticed a pattern where some students are treated more favorably because they engage in light banter or casual joking with her. They get remembered, their names are noted, and sometimes they appear to receive better feedback. I don't do that. For me, studying hard, presenting presentation properly and showing respect through performance should be enough. It's frustrating to see that personal impressions and social strategies sometimes matter more than genuine effort, but I'm just focusing on doing my best. 
This is the first time I find myself agreeing with the negative reviews about a faculty. Normally, I can ignore them and form my own opinion, but with SLN, it's impossible. Her teaching style and how she treats hardworking students has made this course unnecessarily stressful and unpleasant.
She has her good days where she has been kind and nice but God, it doesn't change the overall ridiculousness of this situation we many are subjected to. See less
